title: Fix offline install values.schema.json validation (relax required fields + add defaults)
author: Dylan Brooks
description: Context: During the air-gapped pilots we hit schema validation failures on install/upgrade when using the “minimal offline” values files. The charts were technically installable, but values.schema.json was rejecting inputs due to (a) required fields that are optional in offline mode, and (b) missing defaults for fields that the templates already handle safely. This showed up most often when customers copy only the offline overrides from the docs/runbook (no hosted defaults), and when values are injected by the on-prem installer. What changed: 1) Add safe defaults for common offline paths: - global.airgapped defaults to false - image.pullPolicy defaults to IfNotPresent (offline-friendly) - imagePullSecrets defaults to [] (instead of requiring a non-empty array) - serviceAccount.create defaults to true where appropriate (templates assumed default) 2) Relax overly strict required lists: - Do not require global.imageRegistry in offline mode; accept empty/omitted and allow per-component registry overrides - Do not require external integrations that are optional (metrics exporters, audit log forwarding, etc.) 3) Fix schema typing/oneOf for fields that are frequently set via env var expansion: - Allow integer OR string for select port fields (helm template casts anyway) - Allow "" for optional file/path fields (some customers set empty strings to disable) 4) Tighten only where it matters (kept strict): - Keep additionalProperties: false for the top-level to catch typos - Keep required checks for critical security toggles when enabled (e.g., when audit export is enabled, require destination + credentials refs) Notes: This is intended to unblock offline installs without loosening security-sensitive fields. The signed offline bundle manifest still pins chart versions; this PR only affects schema validation at install time. Testing: - Added a chart-testing job that runs helm lint + schema validation against: a) full default values b) minimal offline values c) values with common SE overrides (custom registry, private CA bundle path, proxy disabled). - Reproduced the pilot failure locally using the same values snippet from SUP-31892 and verified install proceeds. Follow-ups: We should align the docs examples to only include keys that are actually needed; schema changes here are a safety net, not a substitute for clearer guidance.
commits: charts(redwood-private): add defaults for offline-friendly values and relax required list
charts: fix values.schema.json oneOf typing for ports and optional paths
tests: add schema-validation fixtures for minimal offline values
docs: update comments in values.yaml to match schema expectations
changed_files: README.md (developer notes for running schema checks)
conversation: Sahana Iyer (review): The defaults look good, but can we confirm we’re not allowing a blank registry when offline mode is false? If a customer sets global.airgapped=false and omits global.imageRegistry, we should still fail in our hosted-like path.

Dylan Brooks (author): Yep — I constrained the relaxed path using a oneOf on global.airgapped. When airgapped=false we still require either global.imageRegistry or per-component registry overrides. Added a fixture test to cover this.

Connor O'Brien (review): Please add a short note to CHANGELOG about why schema changed; release train needs a heads-up since this is tied to offline bundles. Also, can we link the support ticket for traceability?
Dylan Brooks (author): Added CHANGELOG entry and included SUP-31892 in the PR description + commit message trailer.
Bruno Silva (review): In customer envs we saw empty string used to disable optional file mounts. Schema currently rejects "" for tls.caBundlePath. Can we allow empty string and treat it as unset?
Dylan Brooks (author): Updated schema to allow "" for the optional path fields and confirmed templates already guard with `if` checks. Added fixture `empty-path-disable-values.yaml`.

Sean Gallagher (review): Any risk that relaxing required fields hides typos during install? I like additionalProperties:false at top-level; can we keep it but allow component-specific blocks to accept unknown keys?

Dylan Brooks (author): Kept additionalProperties:false at top-level and in the main component blocks. That should keep typo detection. Where we had to allow flexibility, I added explicit properties rather than opening additionalProperties.
Sahana Iyer (approval): Looks good with the new fixture; thanks for keeping strictness where security toggles apply.
Connor O'Brien (approval): Approved; please merge ASAP so it lands before the next Private bundle cut.
release_notes: Private/offline: Helm chart schema validation no longer blocks minimal air-gapped installs; added defaults and relaxed non-critical required fields while preserving strict validation for security-sensitive configuration.
